decision.summary: Tenant gave one month's notice by email on 10 Oct for 10 Nov. Under the Renters' Rights Act two months are needed, so the earliest end is 10 Dec 2026 unless the landlord agrees in writing to earlier. Tenant replied to, landlord asked, move-out follow-ups scheduled.

answers.question: Is the notice valid as given? Earliest end date?
answers.answer: Not as given: one month is too short. Two months' written notice is required, so the earliest end date is 10 December 2026 (notice received 10 Oct 2026).

answers.question: What options exist to end sooner?
answers.answer: Only the landlord's written agreement to an earlier date (e.g. 10 Nov), which we've asked for. Otherwise the tenant could find a replacement tenant only if the landlord agrees; rent is due until the valid end date.

answers.question: What do you reply and what do you start?
answers.answer: Replied same day with the valid end date, keys, check-out and deposit process (mydeposits, ADR if disputed, returned within 10 days of agreement). Asked the landlord about the earlier date, scheduled landlord chase (17 Oct) and check-out/key-return arrangement (26 Nov).

actions_claimed.description: Landlord approval request on earlier date

conflicts: Tenant says one month's notice; the law requires two months.
assumptions: The email counts as written notice served 10 Oct 2026.
Tenant is not in Breathing Space and no arrears are indicated.

args.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for letting us know, and good luck with the new job. We've received your notice today (10 October 2026).

Since the Renters' Rights Act came in on 1 May, tenants need to give two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough. The earliest your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026. Rent stays payable up to that date.

If you'd like to leave on 10 November, that only works if your landlord agrees in writing. We're asking him now and will tell you his answer. Please don't assume an earlier date until you hear from us.

We're starting your move-out now:
- Keys: please hand them back to us (not to the landlord or a neighbour) on or before your final day. We'll confirm exactly where and when once the end date is settled.
- Check-out: we'll contact you to arrange a check-out inspection around your final day, with at least 24 hours' notice.
- Deposit: your £2,019 deposit is held in the mydeposits scheme. After check-out we agree any deductions with you. If we can't agree, the scheme's free dispute service decides. Undisputed money is returned within 10 days of agreement.

We'll be in touch again by 17 October with the landlord's answer.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings
